# Antibody profiles in organ transplant recipients with and without cryptococcosis

This repository contains the analysis code for a case–control study of 23 organ transplant recipients with posttransplant cryptococcosis and 21 without, recruited at the University of Alabama at Birmingham between 2013 and 2018. It compares cryptococcus-specific antibodies (glucuronoxylomannan- and laminarin-binding IgM and IgG) and total IgM, IgG1 and IgG2 between cases and controls, using logistic regression, ROC analysis, optimal cutpoints and principal component analysis.

The study is published:

> Yoon H, Nakouzi A, Pappas PG, Hemmige VS, Pirofski L. Specific and non-specific antibody profiles in organ transplant recipients with and without cryptococcosis. *Open Forum Infectious Diseases*. 2022;9(7):ofac211. [doi:10.1093/ofid/ofac211](https://doi.org/10.1093/ofid/ofac211)

The analysis website, which explains the code step by step and shows the results, is at:
https://vagishhemmige.github.io/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/

## Running the analysis

The study data are restricted and are not included. With authorized access:

1. Put the study workbook in `data-raw/` (ignored by Git), or change `raw_data_path` in `R/setup.R`.
2. Install the packages attached in `R/setup.R`. `bstfun` is installed from GitHub: `remotes::install_github("MSKCC-Epi-Bio/bstfun")`.
3. Run `R/main.R` from the project root in a fresh R session. Tables are written to `tables/` and figures to `figures/`.
4. Preview the website with `quarto render`. Do not commit `docs/`: when the change reaches `master`, GitHub Actions renders the site and publishes it.

The analysis code is the published 2022 analysis, reorganized into scripts without changing its logic.
